summary: Travis L. Smith specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley under Vasudha Dalmia, Robert P. Goldman, and Sally J. Sutherland Goldman, and earned his PhD at Columbia University under John Stratton Hawley in 2007, later lecturing at UC Berkeley.
Trent Walker works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, where his doctoral supervisor was Alexander von Rospatt.

Trevor Leggett (1914–2000) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology. He studied at King's College London, SOAS, and under Arthur Waley, Hari Prasad Shastri, and Yukio Tani. He served as Head of the BBC Japanese Service (~1946–1970).

Trijang Rinpoche (1901–1981) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied at Gyuto Monastery (1919) and under Pabongkhapa Dechen Nyingpo, among others. He succeeded Ling Rinpoche and taught prominent figures, including the 14th Dalai Lama.
Trine Brox specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA under Christian K. Wedemeyer and was attested as an Associate Professor at the University of Copenhagen in 2026.
Trinle Lhundrub studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
Tro Shul Khenpo Jampal Dorjé studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Troy Organ (1912–1992) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Iowa (~1937–1941). He held positions at Parsons College (~1944–1946), the University of Akron (~1946–1954), Ohio University (1954), and Chatham University.

Trulshik Rinpoche (1924–2011) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, and others, and taught prominent students including the 14th Dalai Lama, Phakchok Rinpoche, and Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.

Trulshik Rinpoche Ngawang Chökyi Lodrö (1923–2011) was a master in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He founded Thubten Chöling, served as official head of the Nyingma tradition in 2010, and taught the 14th Dalai Lama and Sogyal Rinpoche.
Trung Huynh is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. Huynh earned a PhD at the University of the West under the supervision of Darui Long, attested in 2016.

Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche (b. 1968) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute and earned a PhD from Harvard (~1997–2004) under Leonard van der Kuijp, later founding the United Trungram Buddhist Foundation and Fellowship.

Trungram Gyalwa Rinpoche (b. 1968) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Harvard University (PhD 2004), later holding visiting posts at the University of Michigan and McGill University (2016).

Tryambak Shankar Shejwalkar (1895–1963) was an Indian historian and Indologist. He studied at the University of Mumbai (~1913–1917) and later served on the faculty at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1939–1955).

Tryambakarama Sastri worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Lakshmana Sastri Dravida, earned a Vedantacharya from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and served as headmaster (pradhanadhyapaka) at Government Sanskrit Pathashala, Jamnagar (attested 1932).
Tré Khen Zur Lozang Wangchuk studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Trijang Rinpoche, and the 14th Dalai Lama.

Trịnh Xuân Thuận (b. 1948) works in religious studies and other fields. He studied at the California Institute of Technology (~1967–1969) and Princeton University (~1969–1974), and took up a post at the University of Virginia around 1976.

Tse-fu Kuan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich in 2004. He conducted postdoctoral research at National Cheng Kung University and held a post at Yuan Ze University (attested 2015).

Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche (1914–1983) was an active figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a Geshe Lharampa degree at Ganden Monastery, held a post at Ganden Jangtse Monastery, and taught the 14th Dalai Lama and Alexander Berzin.

Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang (b. 1951) is a Tibetology and linguistics educator. He studied at Panjab University, Tibetan Children's Village, and the University of Glasgow (1987). He served as headmaster at Tibetan Children's Village and taught Tibetan at Oxford (2001).
